subject: Recap: Pegasus security call — retention windows, pen-test evidence & next actions
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <security@pegasuspay.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Pegasus security call — retention windows, pen-test evidence & next actions

Alex — thanks for carving out time today. Quick recap of what we discussed and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. I captured the items that matter to you from a security/compliance gating perspective.

What Pegasus said (pain & goals):
- Need clarity on audit log coverage and retention: must see request/response traces for admin/config changes + API calls tied to customer identifiers for 13 months.
- SOC 2: primary ask is Type II report (last 12 months) and a summary of in-scope controls — auditor evidence buckets rather than raw files.
- DPA: standard Pegasus edits are limited to retention and subprocessor clauses; legal will share a redline.
- Pen test: Pegasus requires either a recent third-party pen-test report (past 12 months) or a scoped remediation plan plus dates for an upcoming window.

What Redwood proposes (high level):
- Audit logs: we can provide a sample CSV export (attached) and a short doc about fields and retention scopes. Full ingestion/export access can be arranged to your SIEM under an RBAC account.
- SOC 2: attached is a two-page SOC 2 summary; we can provide a redacted Type II report under NDA / secure link.
- DPA: attached draft with our standard retention clauses — we can accept a 14-month retention window for audit logs with a defined purge process and the ability to scope per-tenant exceptions.
- Pen test: we have a 2026 third-party test and a remediation timeline; if you need a fresh window we can schedule a test for Q4 2027.

Next steps / owners (proposed):
1) Marcus (me) — circulate redacted SOC 2 Type II link and the audit-log sample by EOD tomorrow (09/08).
2) Soojin — technical deep-dive to show the audit exports and retention config; propose Tue 09/14 10:00am PT.
3) Neha — intake legal redline when you share DPA; target internal review in 3 business days.
4) Alex/Pegasus — share a prioritized evidence checklist (must-have vs nice-to-have) and confirm whether Pegasus requires live SIEM integration or periodic bulk exports.

Attachments referenced: soc2-summary.pdf (2pg overview), audit-log-sample.csv (10 rows, redacted ids), dpa-draft.docx (standard).

If that matches your read, let me know and I’ll send the redacted SOC 2 link and calendar invites for the deep-dive.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap: Pegasus security call — retention windows, pen-test evidence & next actions

Thanks Marcus — helpful summary. A few clarifying questions before we lock calendar: 

1) Audit logs — the sample is useful. Can you confirm the retention policy is configurable per-tenant and provide the exact field schema (timestamp, actor_id, tenant_id, request_path, response_code, raw_payload_present(boolean))? We need to validate with our data classification team.

2) SOC 2 — we will need either a full Type II (redacted) or a SOC auditor contact to validate scope. Do you have an NDA workflow for sharing the report?

3) DPA — legal will circulate a redline focused on retention and subprocessors today. Is Redwood flexible on subprocessors for telemetry storage (we prefer to know the storage location and any third-party processing partners)?

4) Pen test — your 2026 report is a start. If you plan a Q4 window, we need proposed dates and the scope (external infra, app, internal staff simulator).

If you can answer (1) and (3) in writing and share the redacted SOC 2 link, we’ll confirm the attendees for the deep-dive. Also: include any compliance attestations (ISO/other) if available.

Alex Rivera
Head of Security, Pegasus Payments

Subject: Re: Recap: Pegasus security call — retention windows, pen-test evidence & next actions

Alex — short answers inline and next actions. Forwarding the SOC 2 sharing steps and a sample field mapping below.

1) Audit log schema (confirmed): timestamp, actor_id, tenant_id, request_path, response_code, event_type, object_id, raw_payload_present (boolean). The retention period is configurable per-tenant via the Console — default is 6 months, we can set to 14 months for Pegasus; retention is enforced via scheduled purges and documented in the DPA draft (see attached). See attached audit-log-sample.csv for example.

2) SOC 2 sharing: we host redacted Type II on a secure S3 link behind an NDA. I can trigger the NDA from our side; alternatively we can send via your vendor portal. Which do you prefer? I’ll start the NDA if we don’t hear otherwise.

3) Subprocessors & telemetry storage: primary telemetry storage is Redwood-managed S3 (US-West region) with encryption at rest (KMS). Subprocessors for analytics/backup are listed in section 4 of the DPA draft; we are open to add an explicit clause naming the partners for Pegasus.

4) Pen test: proposed window Nov 15–19, 2027. Scope: external infra + app + authenticated API assessment (we will provide test accounts). If you prefer a different scope we can adjust.

Next actions (updated):
- Marcus: send redacted SOC 2 link + start NDA flow (within 24 hours).
- Soojin: schedule technical deep-dive for Tue 09/14 10:00am PT — demo audit exports and show per-tenant retention control (calendar invite to follow).
- Neha: review incoming DPA redline and provide commentary (target EOD 09/12).
- Alex/Pegasus: send your prioritized evidence checklist and confirm pen-test scope.
